changes_from_1.0: Protocol 1.0 produced deterministic outcomes (identical results in both pilots, no possible false alarm). 2.0 adds environmental noise to every mode (latency spikes, benign ERROR log lines), two fault types with non-fixed visibility (intermittent_exception, crash_restart), a Docker restart policy for every trial, seven healthy trials per round, Wilson 95% intervals and paired McNemar comparison with the HTTP baseline. Detector rules are unchanged so results stay comparable with 1.0.
study_kind: synthetic controlled technical benchmark; no human participants; no ML
research_question: How accurately can injected faults in a containerized Web API be detected from HTTP responses, container state and application logs, used separately and in combination?

noise.base_delay_seconds: uniform(0.005, 0.05) on every /api/items request in every mode
noise.latency_spike: probability 0.04 per request, extra uniform(0.25, 0.60) s; exceeds the 0.4 s client timeout in about 2.6% of requests
noise.benign_error_log: probability 0.05 per request, ERROR 'Upstream cache timeout; served from fallback', response unaffected
noise.intermittent_exception: probability 0.35 per request of HTTP 500 plus ERROR log
noise.crash_restart: process exits abruptly 0.05-0.50 s after its first /api/items request, without a log line; Docker restarts it
noise.random_source: Python random seeded with TRIAL_SEED ('<seed>:<trial>') plus the container hostname, both recorded

ground_truth: healthy=0, all seven explicitly injected fault scenarios=1, including degraded internal audit functionality even when HTTP still succeeds. Noise in healthy trials does not change the label.
http_rule: positive if any measured request has a transport error or HTTP status >=400
container_rule: positive if Running is false or OOMKilled is true or RestartCount >0 in the post-observation state snapshot; no HTTP healthcheck
log_rule: positive if any application JSON log event has level ERROR or CRITICAL
combination_rule: logical OR of the selected single-source detector decisions
baseline: HTTP alone (standard external uptime/status monitoring); always-healthy is reported only as a reference, not as the baseline
design: Seven healthy trials and one trial per fault type per randomized round (14 trials). All seven signal configurations score the same trial observations (paired, within-trial design). Fresh container per trial. Sequential requests. Five requests are subsamples, not five independent trials. The schedule order depends only on the seed, so every run with seed 2424 has the same order; noise draws differ per container.
invalid_trial_rule: Infrastructure, readiness, Docker CLI or malformed-log failure invalidates the whole trial; retain error and evidence, exclude from metrics and report exclusion count. HTTP connection failure AFTER a confirmed stop or crash is an intended observation.
split_policy: No train/validation/test split: fixed rules, no trained model, no parameter tuned on collected data. Pilot and main runs stored separately. Rules and expectations frozen before collection; changes need a new protocol version and are disclosed.
planned_main_collection: 10 rounds = 140 trials (70 healthy, 70 faulty), phase main, after the 2.0 pilot
limitations: Purposively constructed faults, one synthetic API, simulated noise with chosen rates, low load, local Docker Desktop, deterministic rules. Aggregate metrics depend on the fault mix and noise rates. OR combination cannot lower recall but can raise false positives.
